question: Bhitargaon Brick temple is a good example of the architecture of which of the following periods?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gupta period**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bhitargaon Brick temple is an excellent example of architecture from the **Gupta period**.
 
• Located in Uttar Pradesh, India, it is one of the oldest surviving brick temples in the country.
 
• The temple showcases the **architectural and artistic advancements** made during the Gupta era, which is often referred to as the "Golden Age" of India.
 
• The structure is known for its **ornate terracotta panels** and intricate carvings, reflecting the high level of craftsmanship of that time.
 
• The Gupta period (approximately 4th to 6th century CE) is renowned for its significant contributions to Indian art, culture, and architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Gupta Empire, founded by Sri Gupta, saw a great flourishing of **literature, science, and the arts**.
 
• Famous scholars like **Kalidasa** and **Aryabhata** emerged during this period.
 
• The period is also known for the development of the **classical forms of Indian dance and music**.
 
• Many of the temples and structures built during the Gupta period have influenced later architectural styles in India.
